title: From HR assistant to chief people officer, the career ladder explained with Ledger in 90 seconds
summary: Office-side ladder for business viewers: from the person who files new-hire paperwork to the executive who sets people strategy.

beats.label: title
beats.voice: From HR assistant to chief people officer, the career ladder explained with Ledger in ninety seconds.
onScreen: From HR assistant to chief people officer, the career ladder explained with Ledger
beats.visual: Title scene: full-bleed room, a ladder on the right, the five steps below, small Ledger in the hr2_assistant outfit waving on the bottom step; a dashed arrow climbs to the top; the title card and the 90-second pill appear on the title words

beats.label: rung 1 HR ASSISTANT
beats.voice: First, Ledger is the HR assistant, with a stack of folders.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (hr2_assistant: light-green cardigan, lanyard, a stack of folders, laptop bag). Header HR ASSISTANT. Ledger alone, scale 3.2; arrows pop in on 'lanyard' and 'folders'

beats.label: rung 1 HR ASSISTANT
beats.voice: Then he files the paperwork for each new hire.
beats.visual: A new-hire folder stamped and filed; a leaver folder moves to the archive

beats.label: rung 1 HR ASSISTANT
beats.voice: He also books interviews, and helps with company events.
beats.visual: A calendar books slots; a balloon arch appears for an event

beats.label: rung 1 HR ASSISTANT
beats.voice: So on this rung, he supports every HR task himself.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.06 on 'Supports'

beats.label: climb 1 to 2
beats.voice: After that, he climbs to HR specialist.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 1 to rung 2; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 2 HR SPECIALIST
beats.voice: Now he owns one area, such as hiring, and screens each applicant.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (hr2_specialist: mustard cardigan over a white shirt, headphone around neck, pen). Header HR SPECIALIST. A stack of CVs narrows to a short list

beats.label: rung 2 HR SPECIALIST
beats.voice: Then he interviews them, and passes the best to the hiring manager.
beats.visual: Ledger interviews a candidate; a short list moves to a manager figure

beats.label: rung 2 HR SPECIALIST
beats.voice: So he supports a little less, and starts to specialise.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.3

beats.label: climb 2 to 3
beats.voice: Then he climbs again, to generalist.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 2 to rung 3; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 3 HR GENERALIST
beats.voice: As generalist, he covers pay, benefits, training and employee questions.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (hr2_generalist: teal blazer, name badge, notebook, glasses). Header HR GENERALIST. Four small icons (pay slip, health card, book, question mark) circle him

beats.label: rung 3 HR GENERALIST
beats.voice: He also reviews the policies, and recommends changes.
beats.visual: A policy page gets a pen note and a tick

beats.label: rung 3 HR GENERALIST
beats.voice: Then he advises managers on leave and the law.
beats.visual: A manager figure asks; a leave rule card slides across

beats.label: climb 3 to 4
beats.voice: Next, he steps up as HR manager.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 3 to rung 4; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 4 HR MANAGER
beats.voice: Now, as HR manager, he owns the policies.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (hr2_manager: navy blazer, white shirt, lanyard, tablet). Header HR MANAGER. A policy binder with a legal stamp

beats.label: rung 4 HR MANAGER
beats.voice: Then he leads the assistants and specialists, and handles the disputes.
beats.visual: Two team figures in a row; a dispute card turns into a handshake

beats.label: climb 4 to 5
beats.voice: Finally, he reaches the top rung, as chief people officer.
beats.visual: Ledger climbs the ladder from rung 4 to rung 5; his outfit swaps mid-climb to the next set; the next rung tag lights up on the naming word

beats.label: rung 5 PEOPLE OFFICER
beats.voice: Finally, as chief people officer, he reports to the chief executive.
beats.visual: OUTFIT (hr2_cpo: black suit, gold pocket square, glasses, grey temples). Header PEOPLE OFFICER. A CEO figure at a boardroom table, Ledger beside

beats.label: rung 5 PEOPLE OFFICER
beats.voice: He sets the people strategy, and leads HR.
beats.visual: A strategy slide; org chart of HR below him

beats.label: rung 5 PEOPLE OFFICER
beats.voice: Yet he files almost no paperwork himself, and answers for the workforce.
beats.visual: Slider at 0.95 on 'Shapes'; a staff group appears

beats.label: payoff
beats.voice: So with each rung, Ledger supported less, and shaped more.
beats.visual: Five Ledgers on the ladder, all five tags ticked, the slider runs from the bottom word to the top word

beats.voice: To climb your own career ladder, learn technical business concepts at Edlintics.

caption:
From HR assistant to chief people officer, the job changes on every rung

The HR assistant files new-hire paperwork and books interviews, and the specialist screens the applicants. Then the HR manager oversees the policies and leads the team. Finally, the chief people officer sets the people strategy with the chief executive

So each rung up, you support fewer tasks yourself and shape more of the company. Walk up the ladder with Ledger and note which rung you are on

sources.claim: HR path HR assistant or coordinator, manager, director, then CHRO or chief people officer reporting to the CEO, with duties of each level; generalist vs specialist
HR assistant (paperwork, events), specialist, generalist, manager or business partner, director, CHRO (also called chief people officer) with duties
HR specialists recruit, screen and interview applicants; HR managers oversee recruiting, disputes and discipline and supervise specialists; some managers start as specialists

openQuestions: The Lattice and TechTarget pages are career guides, not official bodies (no government career guide for the top rungs); the BLS page backs only specialist and manager. Lattice and TechTarget list years of experience, which the script leaves out (they disagree).

The director rung is skipped to keep five rungs (HR director sits between manager and chief people officer in both guides); the climb line goes manager to chief people officer. Say if you want the director kept and the assistant dropped.
Titles vary by employer and country; the caption says nothing about pay or years
